{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Parse revenue: remove commas and convert to float
df['revenue'] = df['revenue'].str.replace(',', '', regex=False).astype(float)

# Drop refunded orders — they are not valid completed conversions
# Only 'completed' status counts toward conversion rate
df_completed = df[df['status'] == 'completed']

# Compute conversion rate by customer_segment
# Conversion rate = number of converted orders / total completed orders in segment
cross_tab = pd.crosstab(df_completed['customer_segment'], df_completed['converted'], margins=True)

# Extract conversion rate for each segment
# Use column index 1 for 'converted' (which is the '1' row in the crosstab)
converted_count = cross_tab[1]  # number of converted orders per segment
completed_count = cross_tab['All']  # total completed orders per segment
conversion_rates = converted_count / completed_count

# Find the segment with highest conversion rate
best_segment = conversion_rates.idxmax()

# Print conversion rates for all segments
total_completed = cross_tab['All']
converted = cross_tab[1]
conversion_rates = converted / total_completed

print("Conversion rates by segment:")
for seg, rate in conversion_rates.items():
    print(f"  {seg}: {rate:.4f} ({converted[seg]} / {total_completed[seg]})")

# Output the best segment
print(f"\nHighest conversion rate: {best_segment}")"}
